The Campaign in One Sentence Make cold US viewers understand the money fast. Price stops the scroll, reaction earns the watch time, rarity drives comments. 1. The Most Important Rules ‼️ • Target the US audience. Backyard Breaks sells through live streams, so the content needs to reach people likely to watch and buy in the United States. • NO commenting/responding to user comments on posts. • Show the card price clearly on screen. Do not make viewers guess why the pull matters. PRICE MUST BE CORRECT. • Use the tracker value exactly. If the tracker gives a range, use the range or safe wording like "$100K+". • Open fast. The first 3 seconds should show money, rarity, reaction, or tension. • Use the campaign hashtag stack: #BackyardBreaks #BBPulls #Whatnot 2. What Clips Do Best Priority Clip Type What To Look For 1 Huge card value $10K+, $50K+, $100K+, six figures, seven figures. Price is the scroll-stopper. 2 1/1 rarity Logoman, Papa / Padparadscha, Superfractor, Gold Vinyl, Shield. One copy in the world is easy to understand. 3 Massive reaction Screaming, silence, disbelief, standing up, group chaos. Reactions make people rewatch. Backyard Breaks Content Folder: Backyard Breaks – Clip Context Tracker 3. Three Viral Formats Format 1: Price Reveal • Best for expensive cards, 1/1s, Logomans, autos, patch autos, and obvious chase cards. • 0-2s: start with tension or immediate reaction. 2-4s: reveal the card and flash the value. 4-20s: let the host reaction breathe. End: show value/rarity again. • Overlay examples: "$250,000+ CARD PULLED LIVE" / "ONLY ONE EXISTS" / "$400 BREAK -> $40,000 CARD". Format 2: Reaction First • Best for Grant/host losing it, silence, group chaos, or disbelief. • 0-2s: open at peak reaction. 2-10s: show what caused it. 10-25s: replay the strongest reaction moment. End: value + rarity. • Overlay examples: "WATCH HIS FACE" / "HE KNEW INSTANTLY" / "NOBODY SAID A WORD". Format 3: Jackpot / ROI • Best for break cost vs card value, final-pack tension, case breaks, and buyer payoff moments. • 0-2s: show break cost or setup. 2-20s: build the rip. Reveal: slam the value on screen. End: reaction and final value. • Overlay examples: "He paid $500 for this break..." / "Last pack. One card changed everything." / "Break cost: $600 -> Card value: $38,000". 4. On-Screen Text Rules • Put the price in the video, not only in the caption. • Keep text huge, simple, and readable in under 2 seconds. • Two lines max. Do not cover the card. • Good: "$100K+ 1/1 PULLED LIVE." Bad: "Very rare sports card pulled in a break." • If PSA 10 upside is listed, only use it if the tracker says it. 5.
